name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own the VISUAL PRESENTATION of the interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment

name: Facet
text: To achieve our goal of a compelling visual presentation, I propose we prioritize a dark mode design for our interface. This decision will enhance visibility and clarity, especially for users who work in low-light environments, and it's a widely popular choice among modern applications. By choosing dark mode, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially higher design complexity to ensure sufficient contrast and readability. This trade-off is worthwhile, as it will ultimately lead to a more enjoyable and engaging user experience.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Dark mode’s a fine default, but it’s not the only lever for visibility—what about users who glare at screens in bright sunlight? A light mode with high-contrast accents might serve them better. To settle this, we should test both against our actual user data: if 60%+ of sessions happen in low light, dark mode wins; otherwise, we prioritize adaptability.
